facts.statement: Torosteus was an extinct arthrodire placoderm that lived during the Early Frasnian stage of the Late Devonian period.
facts.quote: Torosteus is an extinct genus of arthrodire placoderm from the Early Frasnian stage of the Late Devonian period.

facts.statement: Fossils of Torosteus have been found in the Kimberley region of Australia.
facts.quote: Fossils are found in the Kimberley region of Australia.

facts.statement: The body size and morphology of Torosteus resemble those of Incisoscutum and Compagopiscis, suggesting it may have had a pelagic lifestyle.
facts.quote: Torosteuss body size and morphology are similar to Incisoscutum and Compagopiscis, suggesting a possible pelagic lifestyle

facts.statement: Analysis of bite force suggests that Torosteus was an active predator.
facts.quote: Bite force analysis has suggested that it was an active predator

facts.statement: The large number of Torosteus fossils found suggests the possibility of schooling behavior.
facts.quote: fossils have been found in numbers, suggesting possible schooling behavior

facts.statement: Torosteus is currently classified as a member of the superfamily Incisoscutoidea within the clade Coccosteomorphi.
facts.quote: Torosteus is now considered to be a member of the superfamily Incisoscutoidea, which belongs to the clade Coccosteomorphi

facts.statement: Torosteus lived between 382.31 and 379 million years ago during the Frasnian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Frasnian to Frasnian (382.31 to 379 million years ago)
